verification_report.summary: The proposed compact-curve Gaussian localization theorem is correct under the stated accepted inputs. Part I correctly controls the moving local exponent under q_m=o(m^(1/(2r+1))), identifies the varying-disc kernel, obtains a uniform incomplete-Gamma comparison below a fixed multiple of T_m, controls the remaining degrees by moment log-convexity, and uses the extremal norm comparison in the correct direction to prove the limsup. Part II correctly normalizes and localizes a finite model polynomial, proves coefficient growth is subexponential relative to the fixed-annulus metric decay, constructs smooth logarithmic weights with a curvature bound uniform in t and large m, applies Demailly Theorem 5.1 in the precise (1,1)->(1,0) bidegrees after the L^m tensor K_C^{-1} twist, and passes to the singular limit by weak lower semicontinuity and monotone convergence. The limiting correction vanishes to order at least q_m and is exponentially negligible at z_m, yielding the liminf. The two preserved exact-model reports were read together, and the appended model contains the verified r=1 endpoint correction. The expression overline(z_m)^{,k} in the displayed definition of p_m is an evident typographical comma and was read as the uniquely consistent overline(z_m)^k.
